FlameLens

Explore the science of fire beyond Earth.

An interactive research workspace for navigating NASA combustion investigations, comparing experimental evidence, and learning how fire behaves in spaceflight environments.
Workspace · Technical methods · Research data · Get started

Fire behaves differently as gravity, airflow, fuel, pressure, and experimental hardware change. FlameLens brings these factors into view through an interactive interface built around public spaceflight combustion research. It helps students, researchers, and curious readers move from a question to the relevant investigation, inspect what its records contain, and compare evidence in context.

The workspace connects NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations on flame extinction, solid-fuel flame spread, soot and smoke-point behavior, and smoke or aerosol detection. Searchable source records, interactive analysis, visual experiments, and short learning scenarios make the research easier to explore while keeping the path back to the evidence visible.
FlameLens is an independent research and learning project. It is not a NASA product, and NASA’s inclusion as a source does not imply NASA endorsement.
| Workspace | What it does |

| Investigation Explorer | Search and filter the research catalogue by topic, source availability, data type, and research intent. Inspect investigation goals, hardware and experiment context, local file coverage, source links, relevance evidence, and known gaps. | | Comparison Lab | Select up to three investigations and compare their conditions side by side. Explore shared numeric fields with unit-aware views, inspect row-level values, and see where measurement definitions and experimental contexts affect comparability. | | Model Lab | Explore research-specific virtual experiments for flame extinction, flame spread, and smoke-point behavior.

Adjust conditions, run local batches, inspect supporting records and analysis methods, review data coverage and applicability, and export a track-specific audit report. | | Research Copilot | Ask about indexed investigations and project methods. Follow answers to retrieved source passages, inspect their locators, and explore a source trail related to the question. | | Mission Deck | Work through three fictional evidence scenarios with Mica, the animated field guide. Each challenge focuses on interpreting an event label, a gravity regime, or a measurement target. | | Overview | Get a visual introduction to the research areas and the tools available for exploring them. |

chunks.locator: Explore the workspace › A typical research journey · paragraph 10
chunks.text: Start with a question. Search the Explorer for an investigation, material, measurement, or research theme. Read the source context. Check the experiment objective, conditions, fields, and available files before interpreting a value. Compare carefully. Use the Comparison Lab to inspect shared fields and see how units, methods, and source definitions affect the comparison. Explore a research track. Set virtual experiment conditions, run a batch, and inspect the method, nearby observations, and domain information alongside the output. Follow the evidence. Ask the Copilot or try a Mission Deck scenario, then open the linked source passages and investigation records.

chunks.locator: Explore the workspace › A typical research journey · paragraph 11

chunks.text: The Model Lab uses different methods for each research question. A shared interface presents their assumptions and evidence together, but the tracks do not share one universal target or one interchangeable model.

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 1. FLEX flame-extinction track · paragraph 13
chunks.text: The FLEX workspace reads complete rows from the PSI-69 local table and uses fuel, ambient pressure, initial oxygen mole fraction, and droplet diameter to find nearby cases. Each numeric feature is scaled by its observed range. The normalized distance to case \(i\) is:

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 1. FLEX flame-extinction track · paragraph 14
chunks.text: $$ di = \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}\left[\left(\frac{pi-pq}{Rp}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{Y{O2,i}-Y{O2,q}}{R{O2}}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{Di-Dq}{RD}\right)^2\right]} $$

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 1. FLEX flame-extinction track · paragraph 15
chunks.text: Here \(p\) is ambient pressure, \(Y{O2}\) is initial oxygen mole fraction, \(D\) is initial droplet diameter, \(Rj\) is the observed range for feature \(j\), and \(q\) denotes the query. The search uses matching-fuel observations when available, otherwise it falls back to all eligible FLEX cases. It keeps the seven closest cases and weights each recorded Test end label by:

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 1. FLEX flame-extinction track · paragraph 16
chunks.text: $$ wi = \frac{1}{di + 0.035}, \qquad S(c\mid q)=\frac{\sum{i\in N7} wi\,\mathbf{1}(yi=c)}{\sum{i\in N7}wi} $$

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 1. FLEX flame-extinction track · paragraph 17
chunks.text: The displayed result is the leading source label and its neighbor-weighted support. The labels retain the vocabulary of the source table; support is not a physical extinction probability. The batch evaluation omits the matching FLEX Test # from each query and reports accuracy and macro F1 over the remaining rows. The interface also shows the nearest source test identifiers.

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 2. BASS-II flame-spread track · paragraph 18
chunks.text: The spread workspace uses measured PMMA points transcribed from NASA BASS-II Table 5.1. Query conditions are sample thickness \(t\), width \(b\), number of burning sides \(s\), and opposed-flow speed \(u\). Their scaled distance to observation \(i\) is:

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 2. BASS-II flame-spread track · paragraph 19
chunks.text: $$ di = \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}\left[\left(\frac{t-ti}{4\,\mathrm{mm}}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{b-bi}{1\,\mathrm{cm}}\right)^2 + (s-si)^2 + \left(\frac{u-ui}{19\,\mathrm{cm/s}}\right)^2\right]} $$

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 2. BASS-II flame-spread track · paragraph 20
chunks.text: The four nearest observations are combined using inverse-distance weights with a small stabilizing offset:

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 2. BASS-II flame-spread track · paragraph 21
chunks.text: $$ wi=\frac{1}{di+0.025}, \qquad \widehat{r}=\frac{\sum{i\in N4} wi ri}{\sum{i\in N4}wi}, \qquad \widehat{T}{100}=\frac{100\,\mathrm{mm}}{\widehat{r}} $$

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 2. BASS-II flame-spread track · paragraph 22
chunks.text: Here \(ri\) is the measured spread rate in mm/s; \(\widehat{T}{100}\) is the simple estimated time to traverse 100 mm. Evaluation leaves out the matching NASA test ID and reports MAE, RMSE, and \(R^2\). The input bounds and nearest test IDs are surfaced with each batch so users can see which observations support an estimate.

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 3. Published SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 23
chunks.text: For the SPICE track, FlameLens evaluates the published luminous smoke-point length relationship reported by Dotson, Sunderland, Yuan, and Urban (2011):

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 3. Published SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 24
Technical methods › 3. Published SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 25
chunks.text: \(L{SP}\) is luminous smoke-point length, \(d\) is burner diameter, \(u{air}\) is coflow velocity, and \(Af\) is the paper’s fuel factor. The published correlation uses 55 smoke-point measurements and reports \(R^2=0.90\). FlameLens samples coflow within the paper’s 5.4–65 cm/s domain and displays the paper-reported uncertainty (±5% length and ±10% air velocity) beside the estimate. This quantity represents luminous length; the interface keeps it distinct from soot fraction, smoke mass, and detector response.

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 3. Published SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 26
chunks.text: | Fuel in the correlation | \(Af\) |

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 3. Published SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 27
chunks.text: | Ethylene | 21.2 | | Propane | 18.5 | | Propylene | 6.05 | | 75% propylene / N₂ | 7.65 | | 50% propylene / N₂ | 13.9 |

chunks.locator: Technical methods › 3. Published SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 28
chunks.text: Reference: Dotson et al., Fire Safety Journal 46 (2011), 550–555 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.firesaf.2011.08.002).

chunks.locator: Technical methods › Batch sampling and reported metrics · paragraph 29
chunks.text: Virtual experiment batches contain 5–100 cases. Where the interface sweeps a numeric condition, it uses a deterministic Halton low-discrepancy sequence (bases 2, 3, and 5 for the FLEX condition axes; base 2 for flow sweeps) and clamps requested values to the track’s supported range. This provides repeatable coverage of the selected interval without implying new physical observations. Evaluation statistics are reported alongside the scope and grouping used by that track.
FlameLens organizes bundled NASA PSI tables by research area:

Flame extinction: PSI-69 FLEX liquid-droplet cases and PSI-159 CFI-G normal and inverse flame records. Flame spread: PSI-25 BASS-II, PSI-99 SAFFIRE-II, and PSI-100 SAFFIRE-III records, with the separate BASS-II Table 5.1 transcription used by the PMMA spread experiment. Soot and smoke point: PSI-107 SPICE condition records and the separately cited published correlation. Smoke and aerosol detection: PSI-102 SAME records, kept distinct from soot-production and smoke-point questions.

The Explorer and Model Lab expose source metadata, field roles, units, row coverage, method notes, and relevant source links. The Comparison Lab indicates whether a selected field is available and comparable across the chosen records. The Research Copilot retrieves passages from the project’s local evidence index and links claims back to their source locations.

For the complete source inventory and file map, see data/READMEDATAMAP.md (data/READMEDATAMAP.md). Additional methods, audit notes, comparison rules, and track-specific documentation are in data/ (data/).

This note describes what the Comparison Lab plots and what its eligibility labels mean. Source descriptions and row counts are drawn from the local audit, source catalogue, and the linked NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) metadata. Local files remain unchanged.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Eligibility labels · paragraph 2
chunks.text: Direct field comparison: the same named quantity and unit are present for every selected source. This applies to the selected field only; it does not establish equivalent apparatus, samples, gravity history, or outcomes. Comparable with caveats: a field can be aligned, but definitions or apparatus differ. The interface shows source units and any conversion alongside the original source values. Not comparable: no verified shared field definition exists for the selected records. The Lab still shows their metadata side by side and explains the mismatch.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Eligibility labels · paragraph 3
chunks.text: Comparison of conditions never implies comparison of targets. The available pressure and airflow plots are condition summaries; they must not be interpreted as predictive or outcome comparisons.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Parsing and transformations · paragraph 4
chunks.text: The Lab reads local CSV exports at runtime and parses quoted CSV fields. A value is included in a plot only when the complete cell matches a signed decimal number, optionally prefixed with ~ and followed by the field's expected unit. Blank and non-numeric values are excluded from the numeric marks and counted separately. No row deduplication is performed. Each dot is one parsed source-table value, not one independent experiment or run.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Parsing and transformations · paragraph 5
chunks.text: FLEX ambient pressure is reported in mmHg and converted to bar using:

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Parsing and transformations · paragraph 6
chunks.text: bar = mmHg × 133.322387415 Pa/mmHg ÷ 100,000 Pa/bar

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Parsing and transformations · paragraph 7
chunks.text: The transformation is reversible to the displayed precision and original source strings remain in the row preview. CFI-G approx p (bar) values are labeled approximate and are not treated as semantically identical to FLEX ambient pressure. An optional independent source-scale view preserves each original pressure unit; its rows are visually aligned by relative range and are not on a shared numerical axis.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Field scope and known limits · paragraph 8
chunks.text: PSI-99 / SAFFIRE-II and PSI-100 / SAFFIRE-III: reported airflow can be aligned as a condition because both local fields are labeled cm/s. The SAFFIRE-II file mixes sample, visualization, and note rows. SAFFIRE-III has two configuration rows and no outcome columns. The chart is not an outcome comparison. PSI-159 CFI-G normal and inverse branches: the approximate pressure field can be compared as a condition. The branch-specific datasets and all event codes remain separate; normal and inverse outcomes are never pooled. PSI-69 FLEX and CFI-G: pressure conversion is shown with caveats because the FLEX field is ambient pressure and CFI-G is approximate pressure. FLEX event categories are not automatically binary labels.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Field scope and known limits · paragraph 8 (continued 2)
chunks.text: PSI-102 SAME and PSI-107 SPICE: these are not target-compatible. SAME records smoke/aerosol generation conditions without a paired detector-response series. SPICE records fuel/nozzle/flow conditions without an explicit smoke-point or soot target. Smoke detection and soot/smoke-point physics are distinct tasks. PSI-25 BASS-II: supplied rows include experimental conditions and gas readings, but no consistent measured microgravity flame-spread-rate target. Final gas readings remain post-test values. PSI-159 inverse: the exported table contains 861 all-empty rows. They remain preserved in the source CSV and contribute to the source-row/missingness accounting; only numeric values are plotted.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Field scope and known limits · paragraph 8 (continued 3)
chunks.text: PSI-107 SPICE: 34 exact duplicate table rows are retained as exported. Their replicate meaning has not been established.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › Relationship groups in the Experiment Atlas · paragraph 9
chunks.text: Atlas links describe relationships grounded in the local assignment map or NASA metadata: CFI-G configurations, the SAFFIRE investigation series, BASS-II imagery and PSI-62 analysis, SPICE input data and PSI-60 analysis, SAME and SAME-R, and FLEX source data and PSI-117 CFD. A link does not establish that rows are independent, that derived products are new test cohorts, or that targets are interchangeable. Each group provides a source link and local Explorer record links where available.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › NASA campaign context shown in the Lab · paragraph 10
chunks.text: The research-note cards summarize published mission scope. These counts and outcomes describe NASA campaign reports; they are deliberately not joined to specific rows in the smaller local CSV exports.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › NASA campaign context shown in the Lab · paragraph 11
chunks.text: SAFFIRE-II: the NASA large-scale flammability report describes nine material samples and flow conditions (20 cm/s for most sample tests, with one at 25 cm/s). The local 15-row CSV is a mix of sample records, flow-visualization references, and notes. NASA report (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20170008805/downloads/20170008805.pdf?attachment=true) SAME: NASA PSI describes 30 samples across five materials, with particle analysis and detector response documented as part of the overall investigation. The supplied local file has four numeric condition records and no paired detector-response series.

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › NASA campaign context shown in the Lab · paragraph 11 (continued 2)

chunks.locator: FlameLens comparison eligibility › NASA campaign context shown in the Lab · paragraph 13
chunks.text: All eight locally audited comparison tables are listed in the source library and can be opened in the Investigation Explorer. The initial comparison uses three records (SAFFIRE-II, SAFFIRE-III, and SAME) to make cross-campaign coverage visible. Airflow is shared by column definition, but the SAME apparatus differs, so the comparison is marked with caveats. A two-source SAFFIRE-only preset remains available for the narrower, direct condition comparison.

The Explorer uses a discovery heuristic over the existing investigation catalogue and DATASETAUDIT.csv. It does not estimate scientific validity, model performance, or operational suitability. The evidence behind every result is shown in its detail page.
For the selected intent, each catalogue record receives an ordinal total from 0 to 7:
| Evidence | Points | Rule |

| Candidate target coverage | 0, 2, or 3 | 3 when the catalogue describes the requested measurement family; 2 for a candidate event/related measurement whose semantics or coverage remain unresolved; otherwise 0. This is based on reviewed source notes, not inferred from column names. | | Phenomenon match | 0 or 2 | 2 when verified catalogue text matches the chosen physical phenomenon using the explicit term groups in src/data/explorer.ts. | | Measurement metadata | 0 or 1 | 1 when the source catalogue describes measured or candidate variables. | | Local source file | 0 or 1 | 1 when the audit maps the record to an actual bundled CSV. |

The total is a transparent ordering aid; it is intentionally not displayed as a probability or a decimal score. Missing/unverified metadata earns no points and is identified as a gap; it is never interpreted as zero measurement. A high score does not mean that a source is training-ready.

chunks.locator: Investigation Explorer ranking › Tie breaking and sorting · paragraph 6
chunks.text: Evidence relevance sorts by total points, then local-file availability, then source identifier. Title and source-ID sorts are lexical/numeric respectively. Metadata completeness sorts by the count of non-null indexed fields (materials, hardware, variables, dates, audit rows), then title; this is not a measure of measurement completeness.

chunks.locator: FlameLens data map — read this before using any CSV › Important interpretation rules · paragraph 8
chunks.text: A category folder does not mean the CSV is training-ready. Each dataset README states whether it is a primary model candidate, supporting evidence, or explorer-only. No target may be inferred from a suggestive column name. Decode NASA event codes and measurement definitions from the official data dictionary/report before training. Rows are not necessarily independent experiments. Group by the underlying test/run/sample. Repeated frames, repeated sensor records and explanatory note rows are not independent samples. The raw CSV files are kept byte-for-byte unchanged. Corrected headers, normalized units, deduplication, row-type classification and derived features belong in a separate processed/ area created by the implementation, with provenance.

chunks.locator: FlameLens data map — read this before using any CSV › Important interpretation rules · paragraph 8 (continued 2)
chunks.text: Null is not zero. Missing or unavailable measurements must remain null with a missingness reason. Use the full model-specific readme before touching a dataset. The readmes explain allowed inputs, targets, metadata, prohibited leakage and next data needed. PSI-102 SAME belongs to smoke/aerosol detection, while PSI-107 SPICE belongs to soot formation/smoke-point combustion physics. These are different scientific tasks. PSI-98 SAFFIRE-I, PSI-101 SAME-R, PSI-60 SPICE analysis, and PSI-62 BASS/BASS-II analysis are additional high-value sources listed in additionalofficialsources/. Their official source records are documented, but their original data files were not part of the upload and are not falsely represented as bundled.

chunks.text: Test end: observed category values in the supplied audit include Extinction (186), Disruption (61) and Completion (27). Do not collapse to a binary target yet. chunks.text: If test ends before an extinction event is observed, consider survival analysis with right censoring rather than labelling the record as a negative example. Distinguish visible flame extinction from persistence of cool-flame chemistry.

chunks.text: Self-ext or flow term has values such as SE, FT and -; do not assign class meanings until the source dictionary/report decodes them. burn time (sec) and peak burner temperature are outcome/observation candidates. chunks.locator: Model track 01 — Flame extinction › Modeling plan · paragraph 13
chunks.text: Audit FLEX labels and group IDs; report class counts and independent test groups. Establish a majority-class baseline. Compare regularized logistic regression and a shallow Random Forest for a verified binary target; use a survival baseline if censoring is real and targetable. Calibrate probabilities using group-respecting validation. Report sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, PR-AUC when imbalanced, Brier score and calibration plots. Keep normal and inverse CFI-G as separate experts. A multi-regime model is a later experiment only after compatible targets and leave-one-source-out validation. Apply a domain/coverage gate before predictions. Outside the verified regime, return related NASA tests rather than a numerical forecast.

chunks.locator: Model track 02 — Flame spread and solid-fuel flammability › Additional high-priority sources · paragraph 13
chunks.text: PSI-98 SAFFIRE-I — retrieve raw/analysed video and sensor streams. NASA describes a large SIBAL fabric sample (~0.94 m × 0.4 m), ~20 cm/s airflow, two cameras, thermocouples, radiometers, pressure/O2/CO2 sensors and anemometers. Candidate derived outputs include flame-front/pyrolysis-front position, flame length, temperature, pressure, gas composition and flow. The PSI-98 page lists raw image distortion-grid files and related resources. PSI-62 — highly relevant ground analysis of BASS/BASS-II imagery using two-color tomography, with reported evaluation quantities including flame geometry, temperature distribution, soot volume fraction and flame spread rate. It is derived/re-analysis work linked to PSI-25/PSI-26, not an independent new flight cohort.

chunks.locator: Model track 02 — Flame spread and solid-fuel flammability › Additional high-priority sources · paragraph 13 (continued 2)
chunks.text: Map recovered outputs back to original BASS/BASS-II experiment IDs. PSI-26 / BASS — linked investigation; retrieve its official record and source files, then assess whether geometry, material and measurement definitions bridge to BASS-II. Do not pool solely because the names are related. LUCI — NASA has published a report summary of extended-duration simulated lunar-gravity flammability tests using centrifugal acceleration on a rotating suborbital vehicle. It includes flame images, oxygen measurement, and reported spread/growth rates and extinction information. This is external NASA/NTRS evidence, not a supplied PSI dataset; acquire its original data package and preserve its gravity time history before use.

chunks.locator: Model track 02 — Flame spread and solid-fuel flammability › Additional high-priority sources · paragraph 13 (continued 3)
chunks.text: See data/additionalofficialsources/LUCILunarGravityExternalSource.md. FM² — monitor the NASA lunar material flammability project page for data release. NASA describes cameras and sensors for spread, temperature, O2 and CO2; the page itself is not a dataset. See data/additionalofficialsources/FM2LunarMaterialFlammability.md. SAFFIRE-IV/V/VI and SoFIE can be considered later if official PSI/mission data and rights are verified; they are not in this current bundle.

chunks.locator: Model track 02 — Flame spread and solid-fuel flammability › Model plan · paragraph 14
chunks.text: Deploy the NASA experiment explorer immediately using local BASS-II/SAFFIRE condition records. Acquire PSI-98 and PSI-62 analysed products and identify comparable target definitions. Build a source/mission-aware training table with sourceid, experimentid, testid, sampleid, gravityregime, material, geometry, oxygen, airflow, direction, ignition and target provenance. Begin with regularized regression or a GAM. Compare Gaussian Process / shallow trees only if there are enough independent groups. Report held-out MAE/RMSE in target units and leave-one-source-out results where compatible.

chunks.text: PSI-60 — Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets. chunks.text: Do not infer detector alarms from particle measurements alone. A response model needs paired aerosol-exposure and sensor-output records.

chunks.locator: Model / evidence track 04 — Smoke and aerosol detection › Additional sources to acquire · paragraph 8
chunks.text: PSI-101 SAME-R — NASA reports 66 flight test points and modified diagnostics including M-pass; intended to improve particle morphology/size evidence after contamination problems in SAME. Obtain the final report and reduced data. Keep SAME-R separate from SAME and annotate its instrument changes. DAFT / DAFT-2 — dust and aerosol measurement feasibility work. Useful to model or explain dust-vs-smoke discrimination and background particle confounding, not as combustion-smoke generation labels. Verify actual PSI record IDs and file inventories before ingestion.

chunks.locator: Model / evidence track 04 — Smoke and aerosol detection › Additional sources to acquire · paragraph 8 (continued 2)
chunks.text: PSI-98 SAFFIRE-I — contains smoke transport and environmental sensor streams associated with a large fire; link as an in-vehicle detection/transport evidence source, distinct from SAME aerosol-source tests. SAME data-utilization analysis — potentially useful model/analysis documentation for smoke generation in microgravity. Treat as derived research, not an independent flight campaign.

chunks.locator: Model / evidence track 04 — Smoke and aerosol detection › Dashboard output before predictive modeling · paragraph 9
chunks.text: Show the experimental source, aerosol/material conditions, size/morphology findings, sensor hardware, measured sensor response if available, contamination/limitations and closest comparable tests. If a paired detector response dataset is not found, state that detection performance is not inferable from the local data.

chunks.locator: Research datasets used by the virtual experiment workspaces › BASS-II Table 5.1 transcription · paragraph 1
chunks.text: BASS-IITable5-1NASA-TM-20210011385.csv is a row-level transcription of Table 5.1 (NASA/TM-20210011385, printed pages 56–57) in NASA's Burning and Suppression of Solids—II (BASS-II) technical memorandum:

chunks.locator: Research datasets used by the virtual experiment workspaces › BASS-II Table 5.1 transcription · paragraph 2
chunks.text: Source: <https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210011385/downloads/TM-20210011385.pdf> Source record: <https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011385> Table data describe 20 PMMA burns (M1–M20); 39 flow-condition spread-rate measurements are numerically reported. Tests M6 and M12 state “Not tracked” for spread rate and are not converted to zero or included as targets. Several flow settings occur within one burn. testid is the group key; condition rows from one test must stay together in evaluation. Initial/final O₂ values are test-level endpoints while airflow is changed during a burn. They are retained for context and MUST NOT be treated as simultaneous per-condition measurements or predictive inputs.

chunks.locator: Research datasets used by the virtual experiment workspaces › BASS-II Table 5.1 transcription · paragraph 2 (continued 2)
chunks.text: Measurements are source values, not independent test samples. This compact transcription preserves the fields needed for the spread-workspace empirical experiment runner; omitted table context is in the cited report. NASA technical memorandum is a U.S. Government work. Retain the report citation when using this transcription.

chunks.locator: Research datasets used by the virtual experiment workspaces › SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 3
chunks.text: The soot/smoke workspace uses the published Table 2 fuel coefficients and Eq. (7) from Dotson, Sunderland, Yuan & Urban (2011), based on 55 ISS SPICE microgravity smoke-point observations. This is a published empirical correlation, not a FlameLens-trained soot model:

chunks.locator: Research datasets used by the virtual experiment workspaces › SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 4
Research datasets used by the virtual experiment workspaces › SPICE smoke-point correlation · paragraph 5
chunks.text: Paper: <https://terpconnect.umd.edu/~pbs/2011%20Dotson%20et%20al.%20FSJ.pdf> DOI: <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.firesaf.2011.08.002> Reported fit R² = 0.90. It was fit to the 55 smoke points; this is in-sample fit quality, not independent validation. Fuel factors Af (as published): ethylene 21.2; propane 18.5; propylene 6.05; 75% propylene in N₂ 7.65; 50% propylene in N₂ 13.9. Applicable only to attached coflowing microgravity flames over the studied burner and coflow ranges. Output is smoke-point luminous length, not soot volume fraction, emission mass, optical obscuration, or a safety classification.

chunks.locator: Research datasets used by the virtual experiment workspaces › Local FLEX records · paragraph 6
chunks.text: The extinction workspace reads the existing PSI-69 FLEX CSV without modifying it. Its case-based model estimates the distribution of the literal Test end source terms only. Official meanings and independence of the test identifiers remain unresolved; it does not output extinction risk or a certified flame state.

chunks.locator: Architecture › FlameLens — NASA Fire-Safety Intelligence Dashboard · paragraph 1
chunks.text: Product class: evidence-grounded research intelligence dashboard with a gated predictive-model layer. Primary purpose: make NASA microgravity combustion investigations easier to discover, compare, rank and interpret for spacecraft, station, lunar-habitat, pressurized-rover and future Mars fire-safety questions.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 1. Product correction: dashboard first, predictors second · paragraph 2
chunks.text: The NASA challenge is broader than the original three-model concept. The product must first answer questions such as:

chunks.locator: Architecture › 1. Product correction: dashboard first, predictors second · paragraph 3
chunks.text: Which investigations are most relevant to prevention, detection or suppression in a crewed habitat? What material, fuel, burner, geometry, oxygen, pressure, airflow, sensor and hardware conditions were tested? Which tests differed within one investigation, and which are comparable across investigations? What evidence exists for an ISS cabin, spacecraft cabin, lunar base, pressurized rover or Mars transit habitat? What is missing from the available evidence?

chunks.locator: Architecture › 1. Product correction: dashboard first, predictors second · paragraph 4
chunks.text: The three ML tracks remain useful, but they are a capability within the research dashboard. Detection is also a first-class evidence domain even though it is not automatically a fourth trained model. Do not make the home page look like a prediction form with NASA data added as decoration.

flowchart TD A[NASA PSI investigations, files, reports and papers] --> B[Source registry and ingestion] C[User-supplied CSVs and reference PDFs] --> B B --> D[Immutable raw source store] D --> E[Parser and schema / unit registry] E --> F[Normalized investigation and experiment catalogue] E --> G[Dataset quality and target audit] F --> H[Fire-safety relevance engine] F --> I[Search, filters and comparison engine] G --> J[Model-readiness gate] J --> K[Task-specific models, only where justified] H --> L[Dashboard API] I --> L K --> L F --> M[Evidence and citation index] M --> N[Grounded SI research copilot] L --> O[Interactive web dashboard] N --> O

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.1 Source registry and ingestion · paragraph 6
chunks.text: Every imported source receives a durable record containing:

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.1 Source registry and ingestion · paragraph 7
chunks.text: NASA PSI identifier, investigation title, version, DOI and official landing-page URL where available. Source file name, file checksum, media type, source folder, release/version date and retrieval date. Raw column names, source units, table notes, measurement provenance and license/citation metadata. Parse status, validation warnings and the exact parser version.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.1 Source registry and ingestion · paragraph 8
chunks.text: Support CSV first. Add PDF, image/video metadata and other PSI file types as separate ingestion adapters. Do not silently treat a document, image sequence or derived product as a tabular experiment table.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.2 Immutable raw layer · paragraph 9
chunks.text: data/sourcedata/ is the immutable, physically segregated source layer. The supplied CSVs are each placed under one primary category folder: 01flameextinction/, 02flamespread/, 03sootsmoke/ or 04smokedetection/. Never overwrite source values, change original headings, remove repeated rows or normalize units in place. Record hashes and source encodings. Store interpreted/cleaned tables in a separate generated data/processed/ layer with full provenance. Read data/READMEDATAMAP.md and the per-model readmes before using any CSV.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.3 Normalized research catalogue · paragraph 10
chunks.text: Use source-aware entities rather than one giant flattened CSV:

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.3 Normalized research catalogue · paragraph 11
chunks.text: | Investigation | PSI ID, title, objectives, research area, dates, platform, PI, DOI, version | | Experiment/Test | investigation ID, test ID, sample ID, run grouping, test conditions | | Fuel/Material | fuel/material identity, composition, form, sample geometry, source wording | | Environment | gravity regime, oxygen, diluents, pressure, temperature, imposed flow | | Hardware | facility, rack/glovebox, apparatus, burner/duct, diagnostic hardware | | Measurement | measurement name, value, unit, method, time/position, uncertainty, pre/post-event status | | Data asset | source file, file type, release, checksum, completeness, provenance | | Evidence claim | statement, source passage/page, supporting investigation, evidence type, confidence/limitations

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.3 Normalized research catalogue · paragraph 11 (continued 2)
chunks.text: | | Relevance assessment | use case, scoring dimensions, score version, rationale and reviewer |

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.3 Normalized research catalogue · paragraph 12
chunks.text: Keep the original field name and value alongside normalized name/value. A normalized field must be traceable back to one or more raw fields and a documented transform.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.4 Relevance engine — the dashboard's main ranking feature · paragraph 13
chunks.text: The challenge asks for investigations to be summarized and ranked by relevance to crew fire-safety needs. Implement a transparent, adjustable Research Relevance Score, not a hidden AI score and not a fire-risk score.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.4 Relevance engine — the dashboard's main ranking feature · paragraph 14
chunks.text: Recommended first-pass scoring dimensions (each rated 0–5 with a recorded rationale):

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.4 Relevance engine — the dashboard's main ranking feature · paragraph 15
chunks.text: Safety-need fit (25%) — prevention, detection, suppression or a cross-cutting fire-safety need. Physical-phenomenon fit (20%) — same phenomenon or a clearly stated adjacent mechanism. Environment fit (20%) — relevant gravity, atmosphere, pressure, flow and habitat context. Measurement fit (15%) — measurements useful to the selected question, with method and units known. Hardware / implementation transfer (10%) — diagnostics, apparatus or controls with a credible use pathway. Evidence completeness (10%) — usable metadata, accessible data products, traceable methods and documented limitations.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.4 Relevance engine — the dashboard's main ranking feature · paragraph 16
chunks.text: Relevance = Σ(weighti × normalizeddimensioni). Keep the dimension scores, weights, rationale, source evidence and score version visible. Allow the user to change weights for a chosen use case. A result must explain why it ranks highly and what it does not prove.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.4 Relevance engine — the dashboard's main ranking feature · paragraph 17
chunks.text: Prevention: material flammability, ignition, flame growth/spread/extinction limits, oxygen sensitivity, material form and airflow. Detection: smoke/aerosol generation, particle size and transport, sensor response, sensor placement and background dust/aerosol discrimination. Suppression: droplet or gaseous flame extinguishment, suppressant/diluent effects, configuration, timing and limitations. Habitat transfer: relevance to spacecraft/station, lunar surface habitat, pressurized rover or Mars transit context. It must show the assumed environment and evidence gap.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.4 Relevance engine — the dashboard's main ranking feature · paragraph 18
chunks.text: For lunar/partial-gravity questions, keep LUCI as external NASA/NTRS evidence for simulated lunar gravity and FM² as a NASA data-release source to monitor. Do not claim either is one of the bundled PSI CSVs. Preserve gravity as a measured/time-varying field where available.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.4 Relevance engine — the dashboard's main ranking feature · paragraph 19
chunks.text: A high relevance rank means “worth examining for this research question.” It does not mean “this technology is safest,” “the hazard is higher,” or “NASA has approved this system.”

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.5 Search and comparison services · paragraph 20
chunks.text: Search/filter by investigation, PSI ID, title, safety function, material/fuel, geometry, oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity regime, hardware, diagnostic type, data availability and evidence type. Comparison aligns only semantically compatible variables. For every compared value, show source field, unit, conversion and missingness. Do not turn missing into zero.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.6 Evidence-grounded SI layer · paragraph 21
chunks.text: Treat “SI” as an evidence-grounded research copilot, not a claim of artificial general intelligence or an autonomous spacecraft safety authority.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.6 Evidence-grounded SI layer · paragraph 22
chunks.text: Parse the user's question into a research intent and environment/use-case profile. Retrieve relevant investigation metadata, measured data, report passages and source citations. Build an answer only from retrieved, versioned evidence plus explicitly labelled engineering interpretation. Attach source-level citations to every factual finding and show the underlying investigation/file. Expose contradictions, missing data, uncertain terms and outside-domain requests. If evidence is insufficient, return “not established in the indexed PSI material” and suggest what source or measurement is missing.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.6 Evidence-grounded SI layer · paragraph 23
chunks.text: The LLM must not fabricate an investigation, measurement, DOI, dataset value or causal explanation. Keep retrieved text and model-generated interpretation visibly distinct.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.7 Predictive-model service (gated) · paragraph 24
chunks.text: Model availability is determined by the dataset audit, not by whether a UI tab exists.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.7 Predictive-model service (gated) · paragraph 25
chunks.text: | FLEX droplet extinction | First candidate; 274 supplied records. Candidate pre-test inputs are fuel, pressure, initial O/N/CO/He composition and droplet diameter. Decode Test end (Extinction/Disruption/Completion), observation window, censoring and grouping before fitting. | | CFI-G normal flame | Separate branch; 179 supplied rows. Candidate inputs include fuel, initial XO2/Xf, pressure and verified flow/composition features. Decode SE, FT, -, Hot ignition, TFP and cool-flame timing before fitting. | | CFI-G inverse flame | Separate branch from normal and FLEX; 154 non-empty records in a 1,015-row export with 861 all-empty rows. Filter empty rows only in a derived working view; retain raw file unchanged.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.7 Predictive-model service (gated) · paragraph 25 (continued 2)
chunks.text: | | BASS-II / SAFFIRE-II / SAFFIRE-III | Experiment explorer first. The supplied BASS-II table has no consistent spread-rate target; SAFFIRE-II has mixed row types and unresolved ?-g semantics; SAFFIRE-III has only two condition rows and no outcome. Acquire PSI-98 and PSI-62 analysis products before evaluating model readiness. LUCI provides external simulated-lunar-gravity publication evidence and must stay a separate source branch; monitor FM² for a released dataset. | | SPICE | Target-audit and experiment explorer first. The supplied PSI-107 CSV has fuel/nozzle/flow inputs but no smoke-point length or soot-fraction labels. Prioritize PSI-60 analysed SPICE products.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.7 Predictive-model service (gated) · paragraph 25 (continued 3)
chunks.text: | | SAME / SAME-R / DAFT / DAFT-2 | Separate smoke/aerosol detection evidence module; do not conflate detector response, smoke aerosol properties, dust-sensor qualification and SPICE fuel-flame smoke-point measurements. |

chunks.locator: Architecture › 2. Logical architecture › 2.7 Predictive-model service (gated) · paragraph 26
chunks.text: Model ladder: baseline first; regularized linear/logistic model; shallow nonlinear model only if it improves grouped validation; probabilistic or physics-hybrid model only when sample count, assumptions and validation support it. Use GroupKFold or leave-one-experiment-out; never split correlated frames or repeated observations across train/test.

Mission Overview — fire-safety landscape, current indexed investigations, evidence availability and gaps. Investigation Ranking — user-selected need and habitat context; explainable score and dimensions. Research Explorer — filter/search the investigation catalogue. Investigation Detail — objectives, methods, hardware, fuels/materials, conditions, sensors, data products, limitations and citations. Comparison Lab — side-by-side comparison and condition-difference map. Fire-Safety Atlas — prevention / detection / suppression evidence map and relationship graph. SI Research Copilot — source-grounded synthesis with claim-level citations.

Data & Model Lab — source inventory, field dictionary, data audit, model status, supported ranges and validation results. 3D Learning Journey — scroll-led explanatory story using a small number of relevant assets and scientific visualizations.

Provide selectable contexts: spacecraft cabin / ISS-like vehicle, lunar base, pressurized lunar rover, Mars transit habitat and Mars surface habitat. Store scenario assumptions as scenario metadata, not as measurements from PSI.

The supplied NASA challenge brief states that spacesuit operations can involve 100% oxygen at about 4.3 psi and describes a possible lunar habitat/rover atmosphere at 30% or greater oxygen and 10.2 psi or less. Display these as challenge-provided scenario assumptions with a prominent “scenario context, not a design requirement” note. Users must be able to edit assumptions and see when evidence does not cover them.

The challenge brief also states that current PSI does not contain direct partial-gravity combustion data. E-FIELD may be presented as an electric-field analogue, not as an actual 1/6-g or Martian-gravity test. Do not interpolate an unsupported Moon/Mars safety conclusion.

API returns source IDs, file/page locators, evidence type and limitations alongside content. Data processing and model training run in reproducible jobs, not during page rendering. 3D files are lazy-loaded from an asset CDN, with LOD/compressed variants and static fallbacks. Maintain audit logs for ingests, normalization transforms, score updates, model versions and copilot citations. Provide an explicit disclaimer: research decision support only; not a spacecraft fire-safety certification, hazard-control design or operational procedure.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 5. Deployment boundaries › 2.8 Model-to-data assignment and data contracts · paragraph 32
chunks.text: The source CSVs are segregated by primary scientific track, not pooled. The exact file-to-model mapping and field roles live in:

chunks.locator: Architecture › 5. Deployment boundaries › 2.8 Model-to-data assignment and data contracts · paragraph 33
chunks.text: data/READMEDATAMAP.md — authoritative category map and interpretation rules. data/audit/MODELDATAASSIGNMENT.csv — machine-readable per-source assignment, readiness, target, leakage and next-action fields. data/audit/FEATURETARGETMATRIX.csv — field/measurement role matrix. data/modelreadmes/01FLAMEEXTINCTION.md — FLEX, CFI-G normal and CFI-G inverse. data/modelreadmes/02FLAMESPREAD.md — BASS-II and SAFFIRE-II/III. data/modelreadmes/03SOOTSMOKE.md — SPICE and PSI-60 target recovery. data/modelreadmes/04SMOKEDETECTION.md — SAME, SAME-R and DAFT evidence.

chunks.locator: Architecture › 5. Deployment boundaries › 2.8 Model-to-data assignment and data contracts · paragraph 34
chunks.text: Detection is a first-class dashboard evidence track, although it is not one of the original three ML predictors. SAME belongs here; SPICE belongs in soot/smoke-point combustion physics. Each readme specifies candidate inputs, outputs, metadata, prohibited leakage and the next data needed.

chunks.locator: Design › Visual direction: a scientific mission-control observatory · paragraph 1
chunks.text: The interface should feel like a polished aerospace research instrument: calm, precise, cinematic and information-dense where needed. It should not look like a generic AI template, a crypto dashboard or a neon-purple “vibe-coded” landing page.

Core palette: near-black/navy space background, cool graphite panels, restrained ice-blue/cyan for active data, warm amber for caution, controlled red for fire/suppression context and neutral white for text. Avoid: full-page purple gradients, glowing borders on every card, random floating orbs, excessive glassmorphism, oversized pill buttons, fake terminal text and decorative charts with no data meaning. Atmosphere: subtle starfield, faint orbital lines, instrument-grid texture and occasional orbital parallax. Keep the data surface legible first. Typography: one distinctive editorial display face for large headlines and a highly readable sans-serif for controls, tables and long research text.

Use monospaced numerals only for measurement values, PSI identifiers and telemetry-like labels. Layout: strong 12-column grid, deliberate whitespace, tight alignment, restrained radii and consistent spacing. Large editorial hero sections; compact, precise data tables in the research app.

chunks.locator: Design › 2. Color and interaction tokens · paragraph 6
chunks.text: Color must never be the only way to communicate status. Pair every status with a label and icon.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson · paragraph 7
chunks.text: Make the landing page an intentional narrative, not a stack of generic feature cards. Use scroll-triggered animation and scene transitions, but keep content visible and usable without motion.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 01 — “Fire behaves differently when gravity disappears” · paragraph 8
chunks.text: Full-viewport hero with a carefully lit Earth limb / orbital station scene and one slow-moving 3D ISS silhouette. Headline: Understand fire before it becomes a spacecraft emergency. Supporting text: NASA's microgravity combustion research, organized into evidence for prevention, detection and suppression. Primary action: Explore investigations; secondary action: See how it works. Minimal navigation and a scroll cue. Do not put a fake “AI confidence” statistic in the hero.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 02 — “The flame changes shape” · paragraph 9
chunks.text: Split-screen educational visualization: familiar buoyant flame versus diffusion-dominated low-gravity flame. On scroll, animate the plume from an upward-bent teardrop to a rounded/spherical flame representation. Labels explain buoyancy, diffusion, forced flow and radiation. Mark the illustration as conceptual, not a measurement or CFD result. Interaction: toggle gravity regime and inspect the explanatory labels.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 03 — “Three layers of fire safety” · paragraph 10
chunks.text: Three editorial zones: Prevent, Detect, Suppress. As the user scrolls, an orbital line connects each layer to relevant NASA investigation families. Prevention examples: BASS/BASS-II, SAFFIRE, ACME BRE. Detection examples: SAME/SAME-R, DAFT/DAFT-2 and relevant smoke/aerosol investigations. Suppression examples: FLEX/FLEX-2, CFI/CFI-G and relevant suppressant work. Keep relationships nuanced: a sensor-qualification test is not a flame-growth experiment; a gaseous-flame experiment is not automatically a solid-material flammability test.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 04 — “The evidence is larger than one mission” · paragraph 11
chunks.text: Interactive mission timeline / constellation. Selecting an investigation opens its detail preview. Show experiment platform, apparatus, fuel/material family and measurement types. The timeline must use real metadata. Unknown dates stay unknown; do not infer dates from an ID.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 05 — “Find the closest evidence” · paragraph 12
chunks.text: Demonstrate investigation ranking by a selected use case, with transparent dimensions and visible rationale. Example use case: “Which experiments inform smoke detection in a crew cabin?” Show a ranked list, not a made-up numerical risk result.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 06 — “Compare conditions, not just titles” · paragraph 13
chunks.text: Side-by-side experiment comparison with oxygen, pressure, flow, material/fuel, geometry, sensors, gravity and hardware. Missing values display as Not reported in this source, not 0. Add a clear note when values are not comparable across investigations.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 07 — “Ask the evidence” · paragraph 14
chunks.text: Show the SI copilot retrieving NASA source passages and experiment records. Display source chips, page/file identifiers and a “what is not known” panel. Avoid an empty chat box as the only product demo; lead with example research questions and evidence cards.

chunks.locator: Design › 3. Landing-page story: scroll is a guided lesson › Scene 08 — “A safer path to the Moon and Mars” · paragraph 15
chunks.text: Switch between spacecraft, lunar habitat/pressurized rover and Mars transit scenarios. Show which conditions are supported by existing PSI evidence and where the gravity/atmosphere mismatch remains. Explicitly show “No direct partial-gravity combustion dataset in the current PSI scope described by the challenge brief.” CTA: Open the research dashboard.

Persistent top bar with FlameLens mark, global search, current environment selector, data freshness/source status and profile/help actions. Left navigation: Overview, Rankings, Investigations, Compare, Fire-Safety Atlas, SI Copilot, Data & Models. Main workspace uses one strong focal area, not many equally loud cards. A contextual right rail can show “Why this result?”, source citations, similar experiments and data gaps. Use progressive disclosure for long metadata. A researcher should be able to inspect every raw field, but the default view should not show 40 columns at once.
Use 3D assets to teach a concept or establish context. Do not place 3D objects in every section.

chunks.locator: Design › 5. 3D asset plan › Curated assets / sources · paragraph 18
chunks.text: See ../assets/models/ASSETMANIFEST.csv and ../assets/models/download-links/ for source pages and download shortcuts. Candidate assets include:

chunks.locator: Design › 5. 3D asset plan › Curated assets / sources · paragraph 19
chunks.text: NASA ISS model — orbital habitat / hero context. NASA astronaut model — human scale and crew context. NASA Apollo Lunar Module — historical lunar-surface context only. NASA Gateway Core — future lunar-orbit infrastructure context; heavy asset. NASA Perseverance rover — Mars exploration context, not a pressurized crew rover. NASA Z2 or Mark III spacesuit — spacesuit pressure/oxygen explainer. Poly Haven fire extinguisher model — suppression-equipment visual; source page states CC0. NASA ISS FBX package — authoring/editing source; convert offline before browser delivery.

chunks.locator: Design › 5. 3D asset plan › Use policy · paragraph 20
chunks.text: Download from the linked official/source page and retain its attribution/license note. Do not hotlink third-party binary assets at runtime. Optimize to GLB, compress geometry/textures, create LODs and inspect scale/materials before use. Load on intersection or user action; do not load all models at initial page render. Prefer GLB/glTF in the browser. FBX is an authoring interchange format; convert it offline unless there is a clear reason not to. Provide a poster/fallback image and an accessible textual description. Avoid showing a Mars rover as if it were the actual pressurized lunar rover design.

chunks.locator: Design › 5. 3D asset plan › Educational visuals that should be custom-built · paragraph 21
chunks.text: Gravity-regime flame comparison: a lightweight shader/particle scene, labelled as conceptual. Smoke/aerosol particle transport: controllable particle field with sensor sampling points. Oxygen/pressure scenario dial: data-driven instrument component using scenario assumptions. Suppressant dilution visualization: conceptual concentration field; not a real CFD or validated extinction simulation.

Use scroll progress for chapter transitions and small parallax depth, not for every paragraph. Use IntersectionObserver-style reveal only for meaningful section entry. Prefer 500–900 ms for major scene transitions; 150–250 ms for interface feedback. Keep the page usable at normal scrolling speed; never pin the page for too long. Add a persistent “Skip story / Open dashboard” route. Respect prefers-reduced-motion; replace animated scenes with static diagrams and remove parallax. Avoid flashing, rapid particles, fake loading animations and forced cursor effects.

Prefer axis-labelled plots with units and exact dataset/experiment IDs. Use a fixed color mapping for prevention, detection, suppression and contextual research. Compare distributions only when variables share definitions and units. Mark source coverage, missing data and unsupported extrapolation visibly. For all charts provide a table/download alternative and a descriptive caption.

First meaningful content must not wait for 3D assets. Use responsive images, model LOD, texture compression and route-level lazy loading. Keep a mobile static fallback for complex scenes and a low-bandwidth mode. Keyboard-operable navigation, visible focus, semantic headings, labelled controls and screen-reader descriptions are mandatory. WCAG AA contrast target; never encode outcomes by color alone. Avoid audio autoplay. All animation must be nonessential to understanding the science.
The design is not ready if it relies on visual effects to disguise shallow content. It must pass these checks:

Every chart, ranking and stat is backed by a source or explicitly marked as illustrative. The landing-page animation teaches a scientific or product concept. Typography, spacing, grid and table behavior are consistent across pages. Every interactive element has a real state change or navigation action. Empty, loading, error, unsupported and low-coverage states are designed. No card says “AI-powered insight” without showing the evidence behind it. The dashboard remains useful with all animations and all 3D models disabled.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 1. Product overview · paragraph 1
chunks.text: Name: FlameLens Positioning: NASA microgravity combustion and spacecraft fire-safety intelligence dashboard. Primary users: professors, graduate/undergraduate students, combustion researchers, aerospace engineers, spacecraft fire-safety and systems researchers.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 1. Product overview · paragraph 2
chunks.text: FlameLens turns NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion investigations into a searchable, comparable and interpretable research workspace. It helps users identify evidence relevant to fire prevention, detection and suppression for crewed spacecraft, stations, lunar habitats, pressurized rovers and future Mars missions.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 2. Problem statement · paragraph 3
chunks.text: NASA has accumulated decades of low-gravity combustion evidence. The findings are distributed across investigation metadata, raw and analysed tables, reports, videos, sensors and publications. Users can struggle to discover relevant investigations, understand experimental conditions, compare results across different campaigns and distinguish direct evidence from extrapolation.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 2. Problem statement · paragraph 4
chunks.text: FlameLens should reduce that discovery and interpretation burden without overstating what the data proves.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 3. Product goals · paragraph 5
chunks.text: Make relevant PSI combustion investigations discoverable in minutes. Rank investigations for a selected fire-safety need using an explainable, adjustable relevance rubric. Summarize objectives, approach, fuel/material, sample/burner shape and size, atmosphere, oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity regime, hardware and diagnostics. Compare tests within an investigation and comparable tests across investigations. Explain how evidence informs prevention, detection and suppression. Identify missing evidence and limits, including gaps for partial-gravity environments. Provide an evidence-grounded SI research copilot with source citations. Offer predictive ML only where verified targets and independent experimental data support it.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 3. Product goals · paragraph 5 (continued 2)
chunks.text: Make the research understandable through a premium space-themed interactive experience and carefully chosen 3D teaching assets.

Not an operational spacecraft fire response manual. Not a fire-safety certification system or substitute for NASA engineering review. Not a CFD solver, detailed chemical-kinetics package or validated combustion digital twin. Not a general-purpose chatbot that answers without PSI evidence. Not a rocket/propellant combustion dashboard; the challenge states that these topics are generally outside PSI fire-safety scope. Not a claim that microgravity data directly validates lunar or Martian partial-gravity fire safety. Not a requirement to have three supervised ML models at launch.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 5. User personas and jobs-to-be-done › Research student · paragraph 7
chunks.text: “I need to find which NASA investigations contain conditions similar to my project and cite the right source.”

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 5. User personas and jobs-to-be-done › Combustion researcher · paragraph 8
chunks.text: “I need to compare fuel/material, oxygen, flow, geometry, gravity and measured outcomes without flattening away experimental differences.”

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 5. User personas and jobs-to-be-done › Aerospace systems engineer · paragraph 9
chunks.text: “I need a clear, defensible view of which research informs a fire-safety function and where the evidence does not cover my habitat scenario.”

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 5. User personas and jobs-to-be-done › Faculty / reviewer · paragraph 10
chunks.text: “I need a transparent explanation, traceable citations, source versions, limitations and an exportable evidence summary.”

chunks.text: Show investigation totals by indexed source, not assumed total NASA holdings. Show distribution across prevention, detection, suppression and contextual research. Show data availability and quality separately from investigation count. Show a visible evidence-gap panel (for example, direct partial-gravity combustion data gap as described in the challenge brief). Every metric must have a definition, source and last-updated timestamp.

Select target environment: spacecraft/station, lunar habitat, pressurized lunar rover, Mars transit or Mars surface. Rank investigations with a transparent relevance score and per-dimension rationale. Allow users to tune weights and sort by score, data availability, measurement richness or date. Explain that relevance is not hazard probability or safety certification.

Experimental variables and how tests were varied. Data products, measured outcomes, sample/test identifiers and data-quality notes. Related investigations, publications, DOI and citation instructions.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 6. Core modules and functional requirements › FR-05 — Comparison Lab · paragraph 20
chunks.text: Acceptance: no silent unit conversion, no missing-to-zero substitution, no false equivalence between different targets.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 6. Core modules and functional requirements › FR-06 — Fire-Safety Atlas · paragraph 22

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 6. Core modules and functional requirements › FR-07 — SI Research Copilot · paragraph 25

chunks.text: Research relevance: how closely an investigation informs the selected user question. Data completeness: how much source metadata and measured data are available. chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 8. Ranking and confidence semantics · paragraph 39
chunks.text: Never compress these into one “AI confidence” percentage.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 9. Non-functional requirements · paragraph 40
chunks.text: Scientific traceability: each claim, ranking and prediction is source/version linked. Performance: first meaningful content does not depend on 3D model download. Reliability: clear empty/error states when NASA PSI pages or files are not available. Reproducibility: source hashes, normalizer version, ranking-rubric version, model version and SI prompt/model version recorded.

chunks.text: Time for a new user to locate an investigation relevant to a use case. Percentage of factual SI claims with valid citations. Number of model predictions withheld correctly when outside the supported domain. Lighthouse/accessibility and mobile performance scores.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 10. Success metrics · paragraph 42
chunks.text: Do not use number of AI calls, number of generated paragraphs or number of glowing cards as product success metrics.

chunks.locator: Product Requirements Document (PRD) › 11. Product disclaimer · paragraph 43
chunks.text: FlameLens is a research discovery and decision-support tool. It does not certify spacecraft materials, suppression systems, fire detectors, operational procedures or habitat atmospheres. All operational use requires qualified engineering review and authoritative mission requirements.
